news.title: Oil Prices No Longer Follow Headlines
news.summary: A month ago, a series of news reports said oil flows out of Hormuz had recovered to pre-war levels, pushing oil prices lower. However, the rout did not last. Benchmarks are set for their fourth monthly gain in a row, and no amount of repeating that Gulf states are exporting even more oil than before the war can change that. Because barrels are not the whole story. “What is the price of oil? Eight months into the war with Iran, what should be a straightforward question has become surprisingly hard to answer,” JP Morgan’s head…

analysis.summary: Crude benchmarks are set for their fourth consecutive monthly gain amid the war with Iran, shrugging off reports of recovering Gulf oil exports and Hormuz flows.
analysis.rationale: The text describes ongoing upward price pressure on crude benchmarks driven by the war with Iran, noting that downward pressure from recovering export volumes failed to last.

news.title: ExxonMobil Profits Double to $15.4 Billion
news.summary: ExxonMobil reported $15.4 billion in third-quarter profit Friday, more than double its earnings a year earlier, with its Gulf Coast refineries running at full capacity and diesel prices doing the rest. The company earned $3.72 per share, or $4.23 on an adjusted basis, beating Wall Street's $4.08 estimate. Adjusted net income reached $17.5 billion, making it one of Exxon's most profitable quarters ever. analysis.summary: ExxonMobil reported third-quarter profit of $15.4 billion, more than doubling year-earlier earnings driven by full-capacity refinery operations and high diesel prices.
analysis.rationale: The article reports historical corporate quarterly earnings and refinery operational performance for a single company, which carries no clear directional implication for crude oil benchmark prices.
